inferred_requirements.title: Payment Processing Service Core Functionality
inferred_requirements.description: Provide a centralized software service capable of receiving transaction requests and processing monetary payment transactions.
inferred_requirements.justification: Directly requested in user prompt: 'Build a ... payment processing service.'

inferred_requirements.title: Payment Service Security Baseline
inferred_requirements.description: Establish security controls and defensive measures safeguarding payment execution, transaction data, and service infrastructure.
inferred_requirements.justification: Directly requested in user prompt: 'Build a secure payment processing service.'

inferred_requirements.title: Payment Authorization and Charge Execution Interface
inferred_requirements.description: Expose an API endpoint to accept payment intent parameters (amount, currency, payment source/token) and execute transaction authorization and capture against the downstream payment ledger.
inferred_requirements.justification: 1. Why: The service is commissioned to process payments, requiring an ingestion channel for transaction requests. 2. Why: Processing payments requires a distinct programmatic boundary to validate transaction parameters (currency, amount, payment method) and initiate charge authorization. 3. Why: Without an authorization/charge execution endpoint, no transactions can be initiated, making the service functionally inoperative.

inferred_requirements.title: Idempotency Key Deduplication for Transaction Execution
inferred_requirements.description: Implement unique idempotency key validation and deduplication storage on payment execution requests to prevent duplicate transaction charges during client retries or network failures.
inferred_requirements.justification: 1. Why: Distributed payment networks inevitably suffer from network timeouts, dropped packets, and automatic client retries. 2. Why: Retrying a non-idempotent charge request would cause duplicate deductions from customer accounts and corrupted ledger state. 3. Why: Idempotency deduplication guarantees strict exactly-once payment execution semantics at the business logic layer regardless of transport retries.

inferred_requirements.title: Cryptographic TLS Encryption in Transit and PCI-DSS Scope Boundary
inferred_requirements.description: Enforce TLS 1.2+ encryption for all inbound and outbound communication channels and maintain strict isolation of the payment cardholder data environment (CDE) in accordance with PCI-DSS boundary standards.
inferred_requirements.justification: 1. Why: The prompt explicitly mandates a 'secure' payment processing service that handles sensitive financial and cardholder data. 2. Why: Unencrypted transmission or porous architectural boundaries expose cardholder data to interception, man-in-the-middle attacks, and compliance failure (PCI-DSS Req 4). 3. Why: Cryptographic transport encryption and strict CDE scope isolation are technically mandatory to prevent credential leakage and satisfy security baselines.

inferred_requirements.title: Immutable Structured Audit Event Logging
inferred_requirements.description: Emit immutable, structured audit log events for all state transitions across the payment lifecycle (attempted, authorized, captured, failed, refunded) while strictly masking/redacting sensitive cardholder PAN and CVV data.
inferred_requirements.justification: 1. Why: Payment systems require non-repudiation, financial dispute resolution, and regulatory auditability for every transaction. 2. Why: Diagnosing settlement discrepancies, fraud patterns, or systemic failures requires an immutable, time-sequenced record of all lifecycle events. 3. Why: Structured audit logging (with PCI-compliant PAN masking) is technically necessary to ensure traceability without creating security vulnerabilities.

inferred_requirements.title: Health Check and Operational Readiness Telemetry
inferred_requirements.description: Provide health check probe endpoints (/healthz, /readyz) and runtime operational metrics to support high-availability orchestration and payment service monitoring.
inferred_requirements.justification: Standard architectural property supporting continuous uptime, load-balancer routing, and failure recovery in high-reliability financial service deployments.

inferred_requirements.title: Target Payment Rail and Gateway Provider Specification
inferred_requirements.description: Specification of downstream payment settlement rail and provider integration (e.g., Stripe, Adyen, Braintree, ISO 8583 Card Network, or ACH/SEPA direct bank rails).
inferred_requirements.justification: Unstated in user prompt. Target provider, integration protocol (REST, ISO 8583, AS2), and clearing rails cannot be inferred without explicit business specification.

inferred_requirements.title: Cardholder Data Persistence and Vaulting Architecture
inferred_requirements.description: Definition of cardholder data handling architecture: PCI-DSS Level 1 PAN storage vault with HSM encryption vs. client-side hosted tokenization (zero PAN storage scope).
inferred_requirements.justification: Unstated in user prompt. The persistence strategy for sensitive payment credentials fundamentally changes architectural compliance scope and cannot be assumed.

inferred_requirements.title: Multi-Currency Settlement and Refund Lifecycle Rules
inferred_requirements.description: Business rules governing multi-currency conversion, settlement timelines, partial authorizations, split payments, and refund/dispute lifecycles.
inferred_requirements.justification: Unstated in user prompt. Currency handling, FX markup, partial capture policies, and refund workflows depend entirely on unspecified domain business rules.
